### BEI-01: Resilience Index (Pre)

"On a scale of 1–10, how resilient are you? 1 = I fall apart when things go wrong. 10 = I bounce back quickly and grow from setbacks."

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone who bounced back after losing everything.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ A prediction about resilience

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:          Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The Man Who Kept Rebuilding

Meet Thabo.

Thabo is twenty-one. He is in his third year at university. He has a part-time job. He has an online business.

He tracked his time. He saw the leak. He almost lost everything to a phishing scam. He learned about risk.

His delivery service was growing. Ten regular customers. A second bike. He was proud. He had rebuilt after his first setback—when Mrs. October left and he lost a third of his income.

Then his bike broke. Major repair. R450. He did not have it.

He had to borrow from his grandmother. Again.

He sat at Mr. Daniels' bike repair shop, not even pretending to need a repair. Just sitting.

Mr. Daniels let the silence sit. Finally, Thabo spoke. "I rebuilt everything. I saved. I planned. And I still lost. What was the point?"

"You think this is the last setback you will face?"

"What do you mean?"

"You built your business once. It broke. You rebuilt it. Now a customer left. So you will rebuild again. That is not failure. That is business. That is life. Things break. Customers leave. Markets shift. The question is not whether setbacks will happen. The question is what you do when they happen—and whether you have the resources to do anything at all."

Thabo looks at Mr. Daniels. "I don't have resources. I have nothing."

"You have hands. You have a brain. You have people who believe in you. That is not nothing."

Thabo is twenty-one. He keeps rebuilding. He still doesn't know how to stop the cycle.

But he is starting to wonder if there is another way.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden truth about resilience.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of resilience as a muscle
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Thabo Didn't Have

Thabo bounced back. He rebuilt. Again. And again.

But here is what nobody told him: resilience is not a trait. It is a muscle.

Some people think resilience is something you are born with. It is not. It is built. Every time you face a setback and get back up, the muscle grows. Every time you learn from a failure, the muscle strengthens.

But the muscle requires resources. Internal ones—your skills, your mindset, your knowledge. And external ones—people who support you, money to survive, tools to rebuild.

Thabo has internal resources. He has skills from running his business. He has a grandmother who believes in him. He has Mr. Daniels, who mentored him. He has Myah, who partnered with him.

But he does not have external resources. He has no savings. No safety net. No protection.

The next day, Thabo walks past Mama Rose's kitchen. He sees Myah, Nosipho, and Mr. Daniels.

"Thabo," Mama Rose says. "Come. Sit. Eat."

He sits.

"I heard about your bike," Mr. Daniels says.

Thabo nods.

"What are you going to do?" Mama Rose asks.

"Rebuild," Thabo says. "I always rebuild."

"And then what?"

"What do you mean?"

"You rebuild. Then something breaks. Then you rebuild again. When does the cycle stop?"

Thabo does not know.

"Resilience is not just about bouncing back," Mr. Daniels says. "It is about building a life where you do not need to bounce back so hard."

Thabo is twenty-one. He keeps rebuilding. He still doesn't know how to stop the cycle.

But he is starting to understand.
